title: CharacterBody2D slope movement degrades the further out from scene center
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.1.rc1.official



### System information

Godot v4.6.1.rc1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9571) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700KF (20 threads) - 63.81 GiB memory

### Issue description

A CharacterBody2D that moves on slopes will have choppy movement the further the slope (CollisionPolygon) is from the scene center (0,0) on the X axis.
CollisionPolygon and CollisionShape produce identical results.

Some, but not all angles, will cause jittery or slow movement on slopes when further out.
I notice the issue can start around 16,000+ pixels away from scene center on the X axis. The Y axis doesn't seem to negatively affect anything.
The same slope will have no issues if it is at 0,0 and it will have very noticeable issues when over 30k or 100k+ pixels out.

I was not able to reproduce the specific range of angles that slowed down movement consistently from scene to scene, but reproducing the angle in the same scene at a similar distance will reproduce the same problems.

Adjusting CharacterBody2D settings like Max Angle and Snap Length has no effect on this.

Moving at higher speeds make the effect more noticeable . Sometimes the slowing or jitter is less obvious at slow speeds.

### Steps to reproduce

1-Create a basic CharacterBody2D with horizontal movement. (The default template code is fine)
Be sure the CharacterBody2D has constant speed enabled and that the snap length is high enough to handle the max angle for floors (around 70 is fine). A Max Angle above 45 allows more angles to be tested so I recommend something like 70.

2-Create a StaticBody2D with a CollisionPolygon2D child. Make a variety of angles to move around on. (CollisionShape2D rotated at different angles works too, but not as convenient). 
Create a variety of slopes that range between 0 to 60 or whatever you like. 11 to 13 degree slopes seem to stick out as problem angles for me personally but it seems random what problem slopes you will get each scene.

3-Try moving the CharacterBody2D on the StaticBody2D close to 0,0. Should see consistently smooth movement.

4-Then position the StaticBody2D around at great distances to see the difference. Make the X axis 30k to 100k+ pixels out from scene center. Should see certain angles slow or cause jittery movement with negative effects more visible the further out from scene center.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[far-away-slope-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26446062/far-away-slope-bug.zip)
